title: Score diagnostique du coma myxœdémateux
formula:
TheMyxedema Coma Diagnostic Score is calculated by totalling the points from each of the following factors:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thermoregulatory Dysfunction | | |
| Temperature, °C (°F) | >35 (>95) | 0 |
| 32-35 (89.6-95) | 10 | |
| <32 (<89.6) | 20 | |
| Central Nervous System Effects | | |
| Somnolent/lethargic | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Obtunded | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 15 | |
| Stupor | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 20 | |
| Coma/seizures | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 30 | |
| Gastrointestinal Findings | | |
| Gastrointestinal findings | Absent | 0 |
| Anorexia/abdominal pain/constipation | 5 | |
| Decreased intestinal motility | 15 | |
| Paralytic ileus | 20 | |
| Precipitating Events | | |
| Precipitating events 1 | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Cardiovascular Dysfunction | | |
| Bradycardia | Absent | 0 |
| Heart rate 50-59 | 10 | |
| Heart rate 40-49 | 20 | |
| Heart rate <40 | 30 | |
| Other electrocardiogram changes 2 | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Pericardial/pleural effusions | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Pulmonary edema | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 15 | |
| Cardiomegaly | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 15 | |
| Hypotension | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 20 | |
| Metabolic Disturbances | | |
| Hyponatremia | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Hypoglycemia | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Hypoxemia | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Hypercarbia | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |
| Decrease in glomerular filtration rate | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 10 | |

^1^Examples include infection, cold exposure, medication nonadherence, gastrointestinal bleeding, heart failure or myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident (stroke), trauma, or surgery.

^2^QT prolongation, bundle branch blocks, non-specific ST-T changes, heart blocks, or low voltage complex.

how_to_use.why:
- Le coma myxœdémateux est une manifestation rare et potentiellement mortelle d’une hypothyroïdie sévère ; pourtant, le diagnostic est avant tout clinique, sans critères diagnostiques universellement acceptés.
- Ce score est le premier calculateur disponible pour aider à reconnaître le coma myxœdémateux.
- Les scores élevés indiquent une urgence et justifient une intervention immédiate ciblant la thyroïde, tandis que les scores modérés peuvent identifier les patients à risque nécessitant une surveillance étroite.
how_to_use.when:
- À utiliser chez les patients dont les résultats biologiques sont compatibles avec une hypothyroïdie sévère et dont le tableau clinique d’altération de l’état mental fait craindre un coma myxœdémateux, non mieux expliqué par un autre diagnostic.
- Ce calculateur ne doit pas être utilisé chez les patients atteints d’hypothyroïdie légère ou chez les patients asymptomatiques.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Always check thyroid function tests (thyroid stimulation hormone [TSH] and free thyroxine [T4] with or without total triiodothyronine [T3]) when considering a diagnosis of myxedema coma.

 - A normal or elevated free T4 or total T3 generally excludes myxedema coma.
 - While there are some rare exceptions, most cases of myxedema coma are associated with a significantly elevated TSH (generally >25 mIU/L, more often >50 mIU/L, with some values exceeding 100 mIU/L).
- Although clinical features may vary widely, most experts agree that some degree of altered mentation is necessary to make a diagnosis of myxedema coma; to minimize subjective discrepancies, the following definitions can be used when scoring central nervous system function:

 - **Somnolent/lethargic:** Mild reduction in level of consciousness; patients are typically drowsy but easily aroused by gentle stimulation and can maintain brief conversations and follow commands once awakened.
 - **Obtunded:** Moderate reduction in consciousness; patients may require repeated or stronger stimuli to arouse and may appear confused, responding slowly or incompletely to questions and commands.
 - **Stuporous:** Marked impairment of consciousness with a sleep-like state, arousable only with painful or vigorous stimulation; responses, if present, are minimal, delayed, and typically limited to simple movements or withdrawal.
 - **Comatose:** Complete loss of consciousness; patients are unarousable and show no purposeful responses or awareness of their environment.
- Additionally, decreased intestinal motility is assessed based on clinical signs such as abdominal distention or reduced or absent bowel sounds.
- All features associated with myxedema coma are nonspecific.

 - Alternative and precipitating diagnoses should be considered.
 - Consult with an endocrinologist, when available, for concerns or questions.

next_steps.advice:
- Il n'existe pas de critères diagnostiques objectifs et largement acceptés pour définir le coma myxœdémateux.
- Toutes les caractéristiques cliniques associées au coma myxœdémateux sont non spécifiques, et ce système de score est limité par le faible nombre de patients à partir desquels il a été élaboré.
- Par conséquent, il est important de privilégier le jugement clinique et d'éviter de se fier excessivement au score.
- Lorsque cela est possible, une consultation avec un endocrinologue est justifiée.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Prendre immédiatement des mesures pour stabiliser le patient :

 - Assurer la perméabilité des voies aériennes.
 - Administrer des liquides IV pour corriger toute hypovolémie.
 - Entreprendre un réchauffement passif en cas d’hypothermie.
 - Corriger les anomalies électrolytiques.
 - Admettre en unité de soins intensifs.
 - Identifier et traiter les facteurs précipitants, tels qu’une infection.
- Chez les patients présentant des résultats biologiques thyroïdiens et des caractéristiques cliniques compatibles avec un coma myxœdémateux, débuter un traitement par glucocorticoïdes suivi d’un traitement thyroïdien.
next_steps.management:
When thyroid laboratory results, clinical picture, and Myxedema Coma Diagnostic Score results are consistent with myxedema coma (>60 or >25 with a high degree of suspicion), prompt steroid and thyroid treatment are indicated.

- Prior to treatment, obtain a random cortisol level.
- Start IV hydrocortisone 100 mg every 8 hours until coexisting adrenal insufficiency is excluded.
- After steroids are administered, give an initial bolus of 200–400 mcg of IV levothyroxine, followed by 50–100 mcg IV daily until the patient is tolerating oral medication (reduce this dose in older adults, patients with lower body weight, or those with a cardiac history, given the risk of complications such as arrhythmias or myocardial infarction).
- Along with levothyroxine, some experts also recommend administering liothyronine 5–20 mcg IV once, followed by 2.5–10 mcg every 8 hours until the patient is stable and clinically improved (reduce this dose in older adults, patients with lower body weight, or those with a cardiac history).
- One reasonable approach is to start with levothyroxine monotherapy and add liothyronine if there is clinical deterioration or persistent bradycardia.
- Monitor free T4 every 1–2 days to confirm treatment response.
- For patients receiving liothyronine, also monitor total T3 every 1–2 days, ideally measured at the trough before the next liothyronine dose to assess steady-state exposure and avoid transient elevation.

evidence:
This diagnostic scoring system for myxedema coma proposed by[Popoveniuc et al. (2014)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24518183/)was derived and validated through a retrospective cohort study combining institutional data and literature cases.

**Derivation:**

The authors analyzed 21 adult patients (14 with myxedema coma [MC], 7 suspicious for but ultimately classified as non-MC) from their institutions.

All 14 MC patients scored ≥60, while all but 1 non-MC control scored 25-50. Logistic regression showed each 1-point score increase raised MC odds by 9% (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.01-1.16). A cutoff of ≥60 was 100% sensitive and 85.7% specific for MC diagnosis, with an AUC of 0.88 (95% CI 0.65-1.00).

**Validation:**

In the same study, the score was tested on 22 additional MC cases from the literature, of which 16 (73%) scored ≥60 and the remaining 6 (27%) scored 45-55.

**Strengths:**

- This is the first tool for MC diagnosis, which is a rare and life-threatening condition.
- Combines clinical and laboratory parameters.

**Limitations:**

- Retrospective design with small sample size (21 patients in derivation cohort).
- Both derivation and validation have potential selection bias.

This scoring system remains used as a pragmatic clinical tool, though its retrospective derivation and lack of prospective validation warrant cautious interpretation.
